mismatch.message: unsupported level change: makelevel: load_special() has no loader for special level "Rog-goal"

summary: Rog-goal has no production loader. Port its whole Rogue quest goal program after the shared special-level object corpsenm resolver accepts named montype species.

source.branch: Rogue quest goal arrival through makelevel/makemaz/load_special, including fixed map, traps, objects, and monster placements.
callers: wizcmds.c:wiz_load_splua -> load_special -> registered Rog-goal Lua program
dependencies: The full program uses existing level/map/region/stair/non-diggable/trap/monster descriptor paths. Its tin at line 45 sets montype="chameleon". Upstream sp_lev.c:lspo_object resolves montype strings for corpse-like objects: named species are searched in mons and stored as monsndx(pm). Current js/mklev.js object wrapper only resolves one-character monster-class strings; a species name passes through js/sp_lev_object.js:normalizeSpecification and applyObjectFields as a string corpsenm. This shared object-descriptor contract overlaps parked C172 adjudication. Do not implement or reserve sp_lev.c:lspo_object until C172 is resolved.

evidence: Saved v36 evaluation at 07a7711f3c33616a45a45bdd323eee7001502b7c reports 19/60 screens and 41 remaining; first stop is the unregistered Rog-goal loader at zero-based step 19. A fresh one-case replay at current commit 115aee92a9578b5bf9b2a50fc88de8c228993522 reproduces the same stop, 19 emitted screens, and 60 recorded steps. Its replay input digest is 6716cbe410e459f68b6b808b43f0a596735361eb079d0f3079311701d3b8c1b5. Manifest, recording and recipe digests match the saved queue. No C recording was made during this investigation.

Read the complete dat/Rog-goal.lua (upstream checkout path nethack-c/upstream/dat/Rog-goal.lua), lines 1-110; SHA256 4a9526d60f6802525e9964e428a5a15afef9d334441dd6c7e9ed8d1bad24d83e. It builds a solid-fill 76-column quest map, sets mazelevel and noteleport, lights the entire level, chooses an up stair in region 1,0..15,20 excluding 1,18..4,20, marks the map non-diggable, places a fixed spiked pit at 37,7, then the named key, named chameleon tin, 14 random objects, 11 random traps, and the listed fixed/random hostile monster descriptors. Preserve declaration order and map spaces for exact RNG and terrain behavior.

Upstream sp_lev.c:lspo_object at lines 3557-3650 reads montype for statue, egg, corpse, tin, and figurine objects; the named-species branch scans mons names and stores the species index. In current JavaScript, js/mklev.js around lines 4586-4604 converts only one-character classes before forwarding corpsenm; js/sp_lev_object.js normalizeSpecification and applyObjectFields consume that field. Thus the source-level prerequisite is the shared lspo_object montype species-name path, specifically exercised by the tin descriptor at Rog-goal.lua:45. C172 already owns the overlapping source gate and is parked for central adjudication; this task is parked until that ownership decision clears.

The missing Rog-goal registration is directly visible in js/quest_levels.js. Once the shared descriptor dependency is resolved, a lua-port should add the production caller registration and port the entire program; independent direct loads should cover Rogue role with relevant alignment variation and validate the tin species, object/trap order, flags, coordinates, monster descriptors, and complete replay. This investigation claims no completed source behavior and does not propose unrelated helper completion.
